fields.description:
## Context

DSO's LLM code review pipeline produces multi-cycle PRs that fail to converge. Empirical evidence (PR #65 escalated to user after 4 rounds with explicit "findings have not converged"; PR #62 oscillated 8->8->6 across 3 rounds; ~10-12 of ~50 post-feature PRs took >2 cycles; admin-merge-with-failure on #45 and #65) traces to four interlocking architectural causes: reviewers stateless across cycles, broken CI/local prompt parity, mid-resolution tier ratcheting that introduces fresh-perspective findings, and lack of a structured terminator for sustained disagreement. This epic ships statefulness, parity, arbitration, and tier-decoupling so reframing-oscillation and local-vs-CI divergence stop driving cycle counts.

## Success Criteria

1. **Stateful re-review with reviewer self-declared relations.** Cycle-N+1 reviewer dispatches receive `prior_findings.json` and `defenses[]` as out-of-band context. The reviewer schema requires per-finding `relation` (one of: NEW_INTRODUCED, NEW_PRE_EXISTING, RESUSTAIN_OF, REFRAME_OF) and (when relation references a prior finding) `prior_finding_id`. The reviewer self-declares the match using its semantic understanding of the diff and prior findings. Findings with `relation: NEW_PRE_EXISTING` (lines unchanged since cycle N) auto-downgrade to `minor` unless the reviewer also references a prior_finding_id justifying re-elevation. NEW_INTRODUCED (lines in cycle-N fix delta) are unrestricted to catch fix-induced regressions.

2. **Single source of truth for review prompts (CI/local parity).** `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/dispatch.py`'s hardcoded 5-line system prompt is replaced with a path that loads the same `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-*.md` files used by `/dso:review`. CI uses the same classifier (`review-complexity-classifier.sh`, not `classifier.py`), the same overlay dispatch (security/perf/test_quality), the same schema validation (`write-reviewer-findings.sh` equivalent), the same severity rubric and NOT-flag rules from `reviewer-base.md`, and the same deep-tier opus arch synthesis. CI delta is limited to the existing `REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci` injection (already shipped by 6da2-4cff) and worktree-vs-CI artifact path resolution. Local-passes-CI-fails as a structural class is eliminated.

3. **Defenses store with split backends, shared loader/writer, and ticket-binding integrity.** A shared `DefenseStore` interface has two backends: `TrackerDefenseStore` (writes to ticket comments — used by `/dso:review`) and `GitHubPRDefenseStore` (writes to PR comments — used by CI). Both backends serialize the same record shape (fields: `prior_finding_id`, `cited_lines_fingerprint`, `defense_text`, `defender`, `cycle_number`, `timestamp`, optional `arbiter_ruling`). Schema and storage are documented at `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md`. Local review without a session-bound ticket fails with a clear error pointing to the ticket-binding rule. At PR open, all tracker defenses for the PR's tickets are mirrored as PR comments via a one-way sync; thereafter PR comments are authoritative for that PR and CI cycles append only to PR. Reviewer-base.md L266-275 (the inline `# REVIEW-DEFENSE:` evaluation guidance) is replaced with structured-defenses-loader guidance.

4. **Opus arbiter on RESUSTAIN-against-defended-ID with trinary authority and durable binding.** When a finding ID `X` is defended in cycle N (defense recorded in the store) and re-raised in cycle N+1 by the reviewer (relation: RESUSTAIN_OF X), the orchestrator dispatches a single opus arbiter agent (new agent file: `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-arbiter.md`). Inputs: the finding, the defense, the cited diff hunks, the `reviewer-base.md` severity rubric and NOT-flag rules. Trinary output: `SUSTAIN_AT_SEVERITY` (uphold reviewer), `ACCEPT_DEFENSE` (dismiss), or `DOWNGRADE_TO_<severity>` (real concern, lower severity than reviewer asserted). The decision is recorded as a defense record with `arbiter: true` and `cited_lines_fingerprint` snapshotted at decision time. Binding is durable for that finding ID at that fingerprint: subsequent cycles must not re-raise this ID against this code state. If the cited lines change in a later cycle, the reviewer's NEW_INTRODUCED authority applies and produces a fresh finding with a fresh ID.

5. **Tier upgrade decoupled from cycle-attempt count.** Tier upgrades occur exclusively on explicit `ESCALATE_REVIEW` from the resolution sub-agent (intent gap, scope drift, classifier-base mismatch evidence). The PASS_NUM>=2 light->standard ratchet (REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md L945-947) and the MAX_ATTEMPTS->deep upgrade (L1072) are removed. `review.max_resolution_attempts` is retained as a backstop but rarely reached because the arbiter (SC4) terminates the dominant disagreement-loop pathology.

6. **One-shot migration commit and validation.** A migration script scans the repo for `# REVIEW-DEFENSE:` source comments, extracts each into a defense record bound to its originating ticket via `git blame`->commit->ticket inference (best-effort with manual-fallback for ambiguous cases), writes all records to `TrackerDefenseStore`, and deletes the inline comments in a single atomic commit. The migration is auditable (lists every extracted record with its source line and target ticket) and runs once. Validation: re-run the new pipeline against the canonical PR #65 and PR #62 diffs and confirm <=2 cycles to convergence with at most one arbiter dispatch each; plus 3-5 randomly sampled small PRs (single-cycle in old system) to confirm no regression on the easy path.

## Approach

**Sequential implementation in three phases (Option B from brainstorm).**

Phase 1 - Parity (SC2). Rewrite `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` to load the same `code-reviewer-*.md` agent files used by `/dso:review`. CI uses `review-complexity-classifier.sh`, same overlay dispatch, same schema validation, same opus arch synthesis. No semantic changes to review behavior. Pure consolidation. Phase ships as its own PR(s) and provides a stable base for Phase 2.

Phase 2 - Statefulness, arbitration, tier-decoupling (SC1, SC3 partial, SC4, SC5). Add stable finding IDs and the relation taxonomy to `reviewer-base.md`. Implement `DefenseStore` interface with `TrackerDefenseStore` backend. Update reviewer dispatch prompts to pass `prior_findings` + `defenses[]`. Add `code-reviewer-arbiter.md` agent and orchestrator dispatch logic for RESUSTAIN_OF defended IDs. Update REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md to remove the cycle-count tier ratchets and route only on explicit ESCALATE_REVIEW. Local stays on tracker backend for this phase.

Phase 3 - PR backend, mirror, migration (SC3 remainder, SC6). Implement `GitHubPRDefenseStore`. Implement mirror-at-PR-open sync. Run the one-shot migration commit (extract inline comments, write to tracker, delete from source, delete reviewer-base.md L266-275 + review-fix-dispatch.md inline-comment guidance). Validate against PR #65, PR #62, and 3-5 small-PR samples.

## Dependencies

- Coordinate with f61f-7e0a (Per-Story PR Review Structure) — independent and parallel; if A's size gate ships first, this epic still applies. If E's region-split ships, the defenses store loader must be region-aware (defenses scoped by file path filter to the right region reviewer).
- Layers on top of closed epic 6da2-4cff (severity calibration, NOT-flag rules, REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci marker, cited_lines field). The new schema fields (relation, prior_finding_id, cited_lines_fingerprint) coexist in distinct sections from 6da2-4cff's additions.
- Soft dependency on any in-flight CI parity work (5d6e-86a9 if open) — coordinate to avoid double-implementation of dispatch.py rework.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- **Resource: reviewer-base.md and code-reviewer-*.md.** Interaction with f61f-7e0a (per-story PR), 6da2-4cff (closed - severity rubric / NOT-flag / cited_lines). New schema sections (relation, prior_finding_id, cited_lines_fingerprint) MUST coexist without colliding with severity/NOT-flag headings. Gate: build-review-agents.sh produces all 10 agents with all required sections after merge.
- **Resource: dso_ci_review Python package.** Interaction with any in-flight CI parity work. Phase 1 supersedes partial parity; coordinate scope. Gate: `dispatch.py`'s hardcoded prompt is removed (not added to).
- **Resource: review-fix-dispatch.md and resolution loop.** Resolution sub-agent must be updated to consume the defenses store when proposing fixes/defenses (so it can recognize "this is the same concern as a prior-cycle defense"). Gate: review-fix-dispatch.md L82 minor-defense prohibition is retained.
- **Resource: oscillation-check skill.** Stable finding IDs and RESUSTAIN_OF detection subsume the literal-diff-reversal check that oscillation-check performs today. Gate: assess deprecation in implementation plan; until decided, both checks run (oscillation-check is cheap and orthogonal).
- **Resource: REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md FALLBACK path.** If f61f-7e0a Strategy E ships region-split, the defenses loader must accept a region scope filter. Gate: `DefenseStore.load_for_region(region_files: list)` is part of the interface from day 1, even if Phase 2 only uses load-all.
